experience_thesis: A first-party founder experience lens on building ventures with constrained resources: validate real customer demand, prioritise the smallest useful test, sell before overbuilding, learn from operating constraints, and systemise only after repeatable value is demonstrated.

principles.statement: Start with a concrete customer problem and test willingness to pay before investing in a large product or operating structure.
limitations: Founder-contributed principle; not independently corroborated in this public dossier.
Applicability depends on customer access, regulation, product risk and the cost of a valid test.

principles.statement: Use available relationships, partnerships and low-fixed-cost experiments to reduce upfront capital requirements, while making obligations and counterparties explicit.
limitations: Founder-contributed principle; not independently corroborated in this public dossier.
Credit, consignment and partnership structures require suitable contracts and counterparty diligence.

principles.statement: Convert early execution into repeatable operating mechanisms only after the underlying customer demand and delivery process are understood.
limitations: Founder-contributed principle; not independently corroborated in this public dossier.
The correct timing differs by industry, safety requirements and operational complexity.

decision_cases.title: Testing a zero-upfront college-fest retail experiment
decision_cases.context: In 2017, during the founder's first year of college, S Haider organised a three-day college-fest selling experiment. The initial model relied on credit/consignment rather than purchasing inventory upfront; friends helped with final-day selling.
decision_cases.decision: Test demand in a time-bounded campus event using supplier/partner inventory access and direct selling, then use a low-cost promotional stunt to attract attention rather than committing to a permanent retail setup.
decision_cases.outcome: The founder's account records approximately ₹2,500 in sales on day two and approximately ₹55,000 in final sales/proceeds by the end of the event, with roughly ten friends helping on the final day. These are first-party reported figures and are not independently corroborated in this dossier.
limitations: First-party founder account; the figures, exact gross-versus-net treatment and counterparty terms have not been independently audited.
This was a short college-fest experiment, not proof of a repeatable retail model or durable profitability.
Credit and consignment require explicit terms, inventory reconciliation and counterparty trust.

sources.title: Founder-contributed account and project context supplied by S Haider
sources.notes: First-party founder material provided for the Built from Zero experience agent. Individual principles are attributed to this source. This is not independent corroboration.

counter_evidence: This dossier is intentionally limited to founder-contributed experience and does not claim independent validation.
The principles are heuristics, not universal laws; they may fail in regulated, safety-critical, capital-intensive or long-cycle businesses.
transfer_conditions: Use only after adapting to the customer's industry, stage, geography, regulatory setting and downside risk.
Prefer reversible experiments; do not use low-capital tactics where they compromise safety, product quality, legal compliance or fair dealing.

non_affiliation_notice: Built from Zero is an AI experience agent based on first-party founder-contributed material from S Haider. It is not a human, does not impersonate S Haider, and does not imply endorsement by any third party.
failure_modes: A short event can create misleading demand signals that do not persist after the event.
Credit/consignment arrangements can create payment, inventory and relationship risk if obligations are unclear.
A promotional stunt may generate attention without repeat purchase or profitable customer acquisition.
out_of_scope: Audited financial advice or verification of historical sales figures.
Legal advice on consignment, credit or supplier agreements.
